text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Senior Israeli army officer: Draft Hebron agreement identical to one signed by Labour government.
- Harsh messages between Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Egyptian President Mubarak preceded Egyptian press attacks on Israeli leader.
- Managing director of Clal concern quits.
- First vote in parliament today on 1997 budget.
- Jerusalem "Rally for Hebron" draws 20,000.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Shin Bet secret service demanding restraining orders against dozens of extreme right-wing activists.
MAARIV
- Syrian foreign minister says Syria not preparing an attack on Israel.
- Finance Minister Meridor says time has come for difficult and unpopular measures.
- Netanyahu: Foreign investors standing in line to invest in Israel.
GLOBES
- Clal managing director resigns.
- D.S.P. Communications merging with U.S. firm Proxim in $400 million deal.
- Israel's Osem cancels deal to buy half of Egyptian food company.
JERUSALEM POST
- Foreign Minister Levy: Government in distress over Oslo accords.
- Syria is not preparing to attack, Syrian foreign minister says.
- Coalition expected to muster majority for budget vote.
- Thousands show support for Jewish settlement in Hebron.
